newsitem.title: FRANCE: French port grain silos unaffected by truck strike.
newsitem.headline: French port grain silos unaffected by truck strike.

text.p: Grain silo officials in the French ports of Rouen and Bordeaux on Wednesday said they were carrying on "business as usual" despite a nationwide trucking strike.
Truckers were blocking roads across France for the third consecutive day, demanding more money and shorter working hours.
"There are no particular problems to report. This is business as usual," an official for the UCASPOR silo in Rouen told Reuters.
The official said trucks, barges and trains were used to supply the silo.
In the southwestern port of Bordeaux, an official for the Sigma silo reported no disruption to supplies although there were traffic jams on most access roads.
French wheat firmed earlier in the day as dealers worried that the strike might disrupt grain transport to and from French port silos.
Wheat into Rouen for November delivery was quoted at 855 francs per tonne, up five on Tuesday.
The truckers have singled out Bordeaux, whose mayor is Prime Minister Alain Juppe, as the main focus of protests.

There were also road blocks in the south near Toulouse, on the A9 motorway to Spain between Nimes and Montpellier and near Avignon, in the west around Caen, Le Mans and Rennes and on the motorway between Paris and Rouen.
